staticText: Local-first English–Swahili draft phrasebook with 194 embedded app-local entries, nine ambiguity-sensitive usage notes, and a local meaning checker. It has no entry-level source ledger or qualified-speaker sign-off. Optional cloud machine translation requires explicit, non-persistent page-session consent.
boundaries: Treat every local entry as an unverified learning draft until a qualified Swahili speaker and entry-level provenance support it.
Do not describe this inventory as reviewed, a dictionary, exhaustive vocabulary, dialect-complete, or human-quality translation.
Standard Swahili is the primary reference; Kenyan, Tanzanian, Ugandan, coastal, and Congolese or Kingwana wording can vary.
Distinguish Niko vizuri from nzuri, pole from samahani, ufukwe from pwani, and buni from kahawa; preserve noun-class caveats and unchanged valid cloud translations.
Never place raw source or translated text in storage, URLs, analytics, accounts, email, logs, or caches.
